title: Grove's USDS-to-USDC swaps route through the legacy DAI migrator and the Lite PSM at par with no fee
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.3.1 decomposes `swapUSDSToUSDC` into a three-hop path. First the amount is scaled: "convert the 6-decimal `usdcAmount` into the 18-decimal `usdsAmount` using `psmTo18ConversionFactor`." Then USDS is approved to and swapped through `daiUsds`, "the contract that facilitates a 1:1 swap between USDS and DAI." Finally "DAI is exchanged for USDC through the PSM at a 1:1 ratio with no fee, using `buyGemNoFee`."

The notable fact is that **USDS does not swap to USDC directly**. The Peg Stability Module Grove uses is denominated in DAI, so USDS must first be converted into its predecessor. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.4.2 confirms the plumbing dependency from the permissions side: Grove's ALM Proxy "has been whitelisted on the Lite PSM," which "allows it to call `buyGemNoFee` and `sellGemNoFee` on the `MCD_LITE_PSM_USDC_A` contract" — a contract whose very name marks it as Maker-era infrastructure.

Two implications follow. Grove's ability to convert into USDC — the entry point for most of its allocation targets — depends on a **legacy contract and a per-address whitelist granted outside Grove's own governance**. And the `NoFee` variants mean the conversion is genuinely costless, which is why the rate-limit-based controls carry the whole burden of restraint: nothing about the swap's economics discourages doing it repeatedly.

The rate limit is charged in **USDC terms** (`LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC`, decremented by `usdcAmount`) even though the input is USDS, which is consistent with the limits being about the asset Grove ends up able to deploy rather than the asset it started with.
description: USDS is converted 1:1 to DAI through the daiUsds migrator, then DAI is exchanged for USDC via buyGemNoFee, with a decimal conversion factor bridging 18-decimal USDS and 6-decimal USDC.
